public_rationale: Prepublication research found updating, editable representations in natural-language models and accurate state tracking in specialized chess models. Those results matter, but they do not clearly establish the reliable use qualified in this claim. Conversely, limited reliability in particular experiments cannot establish that nobody had achieved such use. The evidence does not settle the qualified observation.
limitations: No arbitrary calendar-year restriction was imposed.
Neither detecting a representation nor documenting failures in a few models settles the whole claim.
The result depends partly on what counts as reliable use of a cognitive model.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models do not produce cognitive models of the world, at least none that anyone has been able to use reliably.
conditions: at least not in a reliably usable way

statement.excerpt: Large language models don’t produce such cognitive models, at least not in a way that anybody has been able to make reliable use of.
statement.document_title: Three ideas from linguistics that everyone in AI should know

from_speaker: a persisting but dynamic sense of the world
at least not in a way that anybody has been able to make reliable use of
our_interpretation: Assess whether reliable use had been demonstrated by publication, including earlier demonstrations without an arbitrary starting year.
A cognitive model here maintains and updates representations of entities, their properties, and their relationships as a discourse unfolds.
Reliable use means repeatable use of those representations for understanding, inference, or action. Decoding information from hidden states alone is insufficient.
A bounded research demonstration can qualify; commercial deployment, human equivalence, and memory across separate sessions are not required.
The target period is the accumulated demonstration record through 2022-06-22. Research capabilities have no quarterly reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive contemporary assessment establishes that available demonstrations had not achieved reliable functional use of LLM-produced, dynamically updated world representations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one demonstration available by publication reliably uses a natural-language LLM's own updating representations of entities and relationships for understanding, inference, or action.

evidence.excerpt: These internal representations are structured, interpretably localized, and editable.
evidence.locator: Section 6, Conclusion; reliability qualifications in Section 5
evidence.explanation: Li, Nye, and Andreas demonstrate state representations and interventions in BART and T5, which challenges a simple absence claim. Their limitations section reports complete-state recovery of only 53.8% even in the best case and leaves richer situations untested, so reliable functional use remains unsettled.

evidence.excerpt: Unlike natural language, chess notations describe a simple, constrained, and deterministic domain.
evidence.explanation: The authors report accurate piece tracking and legal-move prediction from move sequences. This is relevant evidence of functional state tracking, but the specialized chess setting does not establish reliable cognitive-model use by the natural-language LLMs discussed in the post.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A prepublication demonstration with reproducible downstream use and reliability measurements for an LLM-produced updating world model, or a comprehensive contemporary assessment establishing the absence of such demonstrations.
